caption:
Google Play will soon ask every Android developer one question: are you a trader?

What happened: International Cyber Digest (@IntCyberDigest) reported that Google Play will show some solo developers' phone numbers and addresses. Google's help page says every account must declare by 1 February 2027 whether it is a "trader" under EU and UK law. A trader on a personal account has a phone number and address shown publicly on Google Play. Missing the deadline can block updates or get apps removed. Developers who do not distribute in the EEA or UK can declare as non-traders.

Why it matters for you: Many students publish their first app from a personal account. Google lists ads and in-app purchases as signs of a profit motive, so a college app with ads may count. If you build from home, that address is your home.

Takeaway: Read a platform's developer policy before you publish, and check what it shows publicly.

Would you put your home address on a public app page?
